title: Save-and-return is wired via a server-side draft table or a client-side local buffer with a sync tick; the pack refuses to ship if neither is present
asA: operator who has partially completed a wizard and will return later
iWant: my partial answers persisted between steps and across sessions, either to a server-side draft table or to a local buffer that surfaces a sync tick when it writes
soThat: closing the tab or losing the network mid-way does not force me to start again from the first step

acceptanceCriteria.description: On ?draft-store=server, entering an answer on step 1 and advancing issues a POST /drafts request whose body carries the operator identifier, the wizard slug, the step slug and the answer field; a subsequent GET /drafts on the same operator returns the persisted answer (the pack drives step 1, types into a field, advances, then re-issues a fresh GET /drafts and reads the JSON body). On ?draft-store=local, the same input path writes into window.localStorage under a namespaced key (draft:<wizard-slug>:<step-slug>) and renders a [data-sync-tick] element carrying an ISO-8601 timestamp updated on every write. When both transports are absent (?draft-store=none) the pack fails at severity block naming the missing transport.

When the draft transport is server-side and the POST returns a non-2xx or times out, the wizard preserves in-memory answers, surfaces a visible unsaved banner (data-draft-state=unsaved) and never emits the sync-tick indicator; the retry stays keyboard-reachable.
acceptanceCriteria.given: server-side draft transport applied and the POST returns a non-2xx or times out
acceptanceCriteria.then: the answers stay in memory, a data-draft-state=unsaved banner renders, no data-draft-state=synced tick appears and a retry control is keyboard-reachable

acceptanceCriteria.description: When the draft transport is client-side localStorage and the write is denied (quota exceeded or a privacy-mode denial), the wizard preserves in-memory answers, surfaces a visible unsaved banner naming the storage refusal and offers the applied fallback (server-side if configured, otherwise a plain in-session mode).
acceptanceCriteria.given: client-side localStorage draft transport and a denied setItem
acceptanceCriteria.then: the answers stay in memory, a data-draft-state=unsaved banner names the storage refusal and any configured fallback is offered

acceptanceCriteria.description: When the draft hydrate on load returns a shape the wizard does not recognise (missing stepStates or malformed answers), the wizard starts fresh, surfaces a data-hydrate-failed=true banner naming the reason and never applies partial answers.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a stored draft whose shape the wizard cannot parse
acceptanceCriteria.then: the wizard starts fresh, data-hydrate-failed=true is emitted with the reason and no partial answers are pre-filled
